message.content:
Each acceleration gives the proton an energy gain of

\[
\Delta E = eU_0\cos\Phi_0
\]

Since the proton is accelerated twice per revolution,

\[
\Delta E_{\text{rev}} = 2eU_0\cos\Phi_0
\]

With \(U_0 = 190\,\text{kV}\), \(eU_0 = 190\,\text{keV} = 0.190\,\text{MeV}\), and \(\Phi_0=\pi/4\):

\[
\Delta E_{\text{rev}} = 2(0.190)\cos\frac{\pi}{4}
= 0.380 \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}
\approx 0.2687\,\text{MeV}
\]

Number of revolutions:

\[
N = \frac{950}{0.2687} \approx 3536
\]

Answer: B
